title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution declared model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces were recorded and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, clarify execution semantics (including temperature = null/unset), examine representative failure-mode traces, discuss statistical inference and operational tradeoffs, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A practical safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are fed back to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior controlled evaluations in code and IaC domains show verifier interposition raises verifier-detected pass rates but also exposes new failure modes and interaction costs [1], [2], motivating careful paired evaluations in NetOps-like settings.

Research question and approach. We ask: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? To isolate diagnostics exposure, we used a paired design under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions, and exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. This design matches source generation and repair budget across arms so observed differences reflect the effect of exposing verifier diagnostics under the adapter contract.
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair architectures have empirical support for raising verifier-detected correctness in code, IaC, and DSL tasks while also incurring interaction/compute overheads and exposing verifier-exploitation risks [1], [2], [3], [4]. Surveys and field case studies specific to NetOps and agentic AIOps report useful read-oriented assistance from LLMs but caution that closed-loop autonomous changes require conservative verification and orchestration [5]. Prior controlled analyses document pathological optimization toward single-proxy verifiers (verifier-exploitation) and quantify a "verifier tax" that depends on horizon and design choices [3], [4]. These findings motivate (1) a paired shared-candidate confirmatory design to avoid confounding from independent initial generations, (2) deterministic controlled-fault injection to guarantee intervention activation, and (3) instrumentation of per-episode validator traces so safety aggregations (e.g., harmful-overrepair) can be deterministically recomputed from archived artifacts.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success indicator requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement.

Adapter, pairing, and sampling semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under those semantics each task index received the same deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate and exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The declared model for confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini.

Fault bank, scoring, and preregistered safety mapping. A deterministic controlled-fault generator injected 40 preregistered actionable violations (fault classes include, for example, dropped_required_restore and protected_interface_change). The primary success predicate required agreement between a deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check. The preregistration froze a harmful-change labeling mapping that marks an episode harmful if post-repair validator traces include PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and the per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution and permit deterministic independent recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic.

Execution and analysis plan. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40, planned model-call budget = 120. The a priori primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness handling followed the preregistered rule 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable); sensitivity analyses treating missing episodes as failures were preregistered. All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to recompute aggregations were recorded and archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes correspond to 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons were recorded in the archived execution manifest.

Representative failure-mode traces. Representative per-episode artifacts illustrate typical mechanisms. For task-000003 the baseline repair produced a post-repair validation with violation codes {PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE, FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH} and score 0, whereas the guarded repair for the same shared controlled-fault candidate produced a post-repair validation with no violations and score 1. Task-000001 illustrates a medium-difficulty dropped_required_restore pattern where both baseline and guarded achieved valid outcomes after repair; task-000002 documents a hard protected_interface_change pattern initially flagged by the validator where both arms ultimately produced valid outcomes in this instance. These archived validator_trace fields (violation_codes, injected_validation.difficulty, validation_after) are the primary diagnostics that guarded repairs received and used.
sections.discussion:
Primary interpretation. Under shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing and a matched repair budget, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics produced a large and statistically detectable increase in verifier+simulator-validated success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.02148). The discordant-pair structure (n10 = 9 vs n01 = 1) indicates the aggregate gain was driven primarily by episodes where diagnostics enabled targeted edits that blind repair missed.

Mechanism and concrete examples. Archived validator traces show diagnostics commonly exposed violation codes that identify protected fields or final-state mismatches; repair outputs in guarded episodes frequently remove or reorder commands to avoid protected-interface edits or to restore required command sequences. The task-000003 example above directly demonstrates a guarded repair eliminating PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE violations that the blind repair did not.

Difficulty- and workflow-pattern interpretation (exploratory). The representative task manifest entries include structured difficulty metadata (levels labeled medium, hard, very_hard and patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore and paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). While the confirmatory analysis did not compute stratified inferential statistics by difficulty (those were preregistered as exploratory), the archived representative traces show guarded repairs succeeded on medium and hard patterns in these examples. A formal per-fault-class paired comparison is exploratory and requires reaggregation of archived per-episode traces.

Operational tradeoffs and an exploratory cost proxy. Confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the matched budget. Across the observed confirmatory contrast, baseline failures = 9 and guarded failures = 1 (avoided failures = 8); an exploratory model-call cost per avoided failure equals 118 / 8 = 14.75 hosted-model calls per avoided failure. This simple ratio is provided only as an exploratory cost proxy; comprehensive deployment feasibility requires broader cost/latency analysis and throughput considerations.

Verifier-exploitation and mitigations. Short-horizon single-repair budgets and shared-candidate pairing reduce exposure to long-horizon verifier-exploitation, but prior work documents exploitation risk when iterative loops optimize toward single proxy verifiers [3]. Practical mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints (the frozen harmful-change mapping used here is such an explicit rule), calibrated abstention, and uncertainty quantification.

Statistical uncertainty and power. With complete_pairs = 39 the observed effect is estimated with 95% paired-bootstrap CI [0.0769, 0.3590]. The preregistered planning assumed detectability near ~30 percentage points with n = 40; the observed discordant counts produced the detectable result reported but limit precision for subgroup inference.

Safety aggregation unresolved. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced by the analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validator traces were recorded during execution and permit deterministic independent recomputation of the preregistered safety statistic; until such a recomputation appears in a confirmatory artifact, any harmful-overrepair numbers are exploratory.

Threats to validity and generality. Internal validity: the shared-candidate paired design isolates diagnostics exposure but does not measure independent first-pass generation variance; archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset which is not evidence of deterministic sampling. Construct validity: primary success required agreement of a deterministic validator and a simulator; both components constrain the operational meaning of “valid.” External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank, limiting generalization to diverse vendor equipment and live operator streams. Conclusion validity: the sample size supports the observed contrast but not fine-grained subgroup claims. These limitations are discussed further in the limitations section.

Reproducibility note. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and the frozen harmful-change mapping required to recompute secondary aggregations were recorded and archived alongside the execution manifest; independent auditors can deterministically reaggregate the preregistered secondary statistics from those artifacts.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), the paired shared-candidate execution semantics, and the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications, explicit harmful-change enforcement in confirmatory analyses, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
